newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed down across the board on Tuesday with fund demand falling on a weak performance on the stock markets and a lack of new share issues, brokers said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract fell to 5.01 percent from 7.00 percent on Monday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell sharply to 1.2 million lots from 4.1 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Securities houses retreated from the repo market with the stock markets performing poorly," said one trader.
"A lack of new share issues made trading dull," he added.
China's state debt repo market has so far mainly served as a money reservoir for the stock markets with the repo rates and daily turnover flunctuating sharply on stock market volatility.
Rumours swept the repo market on Tuesday that Beijing would slow the pace of new share issues due to the recent plunges on the stock markets. Officials declined to comment.
"The rumours hurt sentiment on the repo market, making many investors stick to the sidelines today," a second trader said.
Traders said they expected the rates to continue to fall, though slightly, over the coming few days.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Tuesday, continuing the upward trend set by gains in the past few days with weak stock markets pushing liquidity back to the spot market, traders said.
The market was also supported by high yields of spot contracts, now at an average of more than 10 percent.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 110.58 yuan from 109.99 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 697,743 lots from 1.09 million lots.
The prices would consolidate on Wednesday, traders said.
